Nested Loops

The one idea to landThe inner loop runs all the way through, from its first value to its last, on every pass of the outer loop. So a line inside both loops runs outer count times inner count, and the inner range can use the outer variable to make each pass a different length.

The code, written line by line
The code, written line by line
The solution
Writing it, one line at a time
triangle.py
1num = int(input())2for row_num in range(1, num + 1):3    row_out = ""4    for seq_num in range(1, row_num + 1):5        row_out = row_out + str(seq_num) + " "6    print(row_out)
Watch the program being written, one line at a time.
Line 1. Read N, the number of rows.
Line 2. The outer loop: one pass for each row, from 1 up to N.
Line 3. Start each row empty. This line runs again on every row.
Line 4. The inner loop: count from 1 up to this row's number.
Line 5. Add the number and a space to the row.
Line 6. Print the row once it is built. It sits under the outer loop only.
It prints, for 3
11 21 2 3

Fix: range(1, row_num + 1). range with one number starts at 0.

Exit: one question
Exit: one question
Exit question
Which input prints 12 lines?
A highlights app prints one line for every ball it shows.
highlights.py
1overs = int(input())2for over in range(1, overs):3    for ball in range(1, 7):4        print(str(over) + "." + str(ball))
Which input prints exactly 12 lines?
  • overs = 2range(1, 2) gives only 1, so one over: 6 lines.
  • overs = 3range(1, 3) gives 1 and 2, two overs of 6 balls: 12 lines.
  • overs = 77 counts balls, not overs. range(1, 7) is six overs: 36 lines.
  • overs = 1313 treats every line as an over. That is 12 overs: 72 lines.

Key takeaways
Key takeaways: six examples
Key takeaways
Nested loops, in six examples
1
the inner loop restarts
1for a in range(3):2    for b in range(7, 9):
inner prints 2 lines on each of 3 passes: 6 in all
The inner loop runs all the way through on every pass of the outer loop.
2
count it
1for over in range(20):2    for ball in range(1, 7):
120 balls
Lines inside both loops run outer count times inner count.
3
inner uses outer
1for i in range(1, 4):2    for j in range(i):
6 lines: 1, then 2, then 3
The inner range can use the outer variable, so each pass can be a different length.
4
indentation
1for i in range(3):2    for j in range(2): ...3    print("done")
done prints 3 times
Indentation decides which loop a line belongs to.
5
while needs a reset
1while i < 3:2    while j < 2:   # no j = 0 here
2 stars, not 6
A for loop starts again by itself. A while loop starts again only if you reset its counter.
6
the triangle
1for row_num in range(1, num + 1):2    for seq_num in range(1, row_num + 1):
1 / 1 2 / 1 2 3
One loop for the rows, and a loop inside it to build each row.
